design: Valerian — hourly market-residual signal ladder (1h–7d lookbacks, 1h–24h targets), pooled ridge + GBM twin, Gârleanu–Pedersen aim-tracking controller calibrated to 21 bp, hourly decisions on the PIT 273-asset Kraken panel, graded on daily-aggregated net@21 Sharpe.
lens: NO-FREE-LUNCH / ARITHMETIC (redo the IC-vs-cost line at the mechanism's turnover, breadth, SR0(N); check whether the profit source is honest and whether learning beats a closed-form estimator; check every literature number for gross/net, IS/OOS, market, years; default refuted=true if uncertain).
strongest_objection: The band's required IC looks small only because it is quoted per hour. Restated in the units the record has actually measured, the requirement is the largest signal ever asked of this venue: at HL 6 h the cell must deliver IC_1h 0.037 = daily-equivalent IC_24 0.065 = gross Sharpe 5.3 (0.037 x sqrt(8 x 8760) x 0.54) while paying 82% of gross in fees (34.5 of 42.3 bp/day); at HL 24 h IC_24-equivalent 0.052, gross Sharpe 2.7, 64% of gross to fees; at HL 3 d IC_24-equivalent 0.037, gross Sharpe 1.7. The daily surface has never produced an IC above its |0.059| four-draw noise band (memo E-2), the only hourly-cadence read in the repo (816 H=60, `PHASE1_RESULT.md` grid: gross Sharpe +2.03 at turnover 1.40 -> net -107 at 21 bp) implies IC_1h ~ 0.008 at N_eff 8, and the only published intraday crypto reversal measurement (Kitron-Wengrowicz, 15 min, Binance) is 1.3 bp/trade gross against a 5 bp round trip - 30x short of Kraken's 42 bp round trip. Second, the hourly cadence buys nothing where TASK_915 already reaches: against a DAILY GP-smoothed book on the same signal (which 915 §4.2 specifies), the hourly GP book lowers the required IC by ~4% at HL 24 h and ~0% at HL 3 d - the advertised 22-25% is against a strawman raw daily rebalance. The design's unique territory is therefore HL < ~12 h, exactly where the requirement is highest and where the stale-tape bid-ask bounce (rho_1 ~ -(s^2/4)/(sigma_1h^2 + s^2/2) ~ -0.10 for a 50 bp spread alt) manufactures a large, uncapturable 'reversal IC' - and the design's pre-registered guard against it is vacuous as written (entry at open of t+1 is the same print as close of t on a stale tape; 816's G8 actually enters at close(t+1), one full bar later). So the design is TASK_915 moved to hourly bars: redundant for HL >= 1 d, and for HL < 12 h it needs a gross-Sharpe-3-to-5 conditional mean that every neighbouring measurement (806/811/816/897 below, 819/898 above, K-W outside) says reads 'real, cost-bound'.
arithmetic_check:
VERIFIED (design's formulas hold): with sigma_1h = 350/sqrt(24) = 71 bp and w ∝ z, Σ|w| = 1: gross/day = 24 x 1.25 x IC_1h x 71 x TC = 2130·TC·IC_1h bp; SD/day = sqrt(24) x 1.25 x 71/sqrt(N_eff) = 435/sqrt(N_eff) bp (154 bp at N_eff 8, 29%/yr); +0.97/yr = 0.0508/day => net >= 22.1/sqrt(N_eff) bp/day (7.8 at N_eff 8). AR(1) full-trade turnover sqrt(2(1-rho)) -> 1.41 at rho 0, matching 816's 1.38-1.41 at every H. GP EMA formulas re-derived: TC(theta,rho) = sqrt((2theta-theta^2)/(1-(1-theta)^2 rho^2)), Var(x)/Var(s) = theta/(2-theta)·(1+(1-theta)rho)/(1-(1-theta)rho), Cov(s_t,x_{t-1}) = theta·rho/(1-(1-theta)rho) - all correct. HL 6 h, theta 0.04: TC 0.541, tau 0.068/h = 1.64/day, cost 34.5 bp/day, IC_1h* = (34.5+7.8)/(2130 x 0.541) = 0.0367 - design's 0.037 checks. SR0(N) at SD_SR = 0.667: N=12 -> 0.667 x (0.4228 x 1.383 + 0.5772 x 1.871) = 1.11; N=48 -> 1.51 - both check. Per-hour IC null SD 1/sqrt(N-1) ~ 0.063 and SE(mean IC) ~ 0.0005-0.0009 over 19.7k hours - detection is not the bar; agreed.

REFRAMED (same arithmetic, honest units): (1) Daily-IC equivalent of the required hourly IC, IC_24 = IC_1h·(1-rho^24)/((1-rho)·sqrt(24)): HL 6 h 0.037 -> 0.065; HL 24 h 0.0145 -> 0.052; HL 3 d 0.0084 -> 0.037; HL 30 d 0.0046 -> 0.0225. The memo's daily requirement is 0.02-0.03 and 819 CAPACITY's daily point estimates were -0.010..+0.037 inside a |0.059| noise band - the band demands 1.5-3x the strongest daily IC ever hinted at. (2) Gross Sharpe required = IC·sqrt(N_eff·8760)·TC: HL 6 h 5.3, HL 24 h 2.7, HL 3 d 1.7; fee share of gross 82% / 64% / 44%. (3) Hourly-GP vs DAILY-GP on the same signal (not raw daily): HL 24 h daily GP with rho_day 0.5, theta 0.5: TC 0.894, tau 0.633/day, cost 13.3, IC_24* = 21.1/(437.5 x 0.894) = 0.054 <=> IC_1h 0.0151 vs hourly-GP 0.0145 -> 4% saving; HL 3 d daily GP with rho_day 0.794, theta 0.3: TC 0.859, tau 0.28/day, cost 5.9, IC_24* 0.0365 <=> IC_1h 0.0083 vs hourly 0.0084 -> 0%. The 22-25% claim compares against raw daily re-ranking only. (4) In-repo anchor for 'IC of anything at 1 h on Kraken': 816 full64 H=60 gross Sharpe +2.03 (`PHASE1_RESULT.md` grid) => IC_1h = 2.03/sqrt(8 x 8760) ~ 0.008 at N_eff 8 (0.005 at N_eff 20), with rho ~ 0 persistence (turnover 1.40) - one fifth of the HL-6h line and uncapturable by smoothing; native lookback features are a different set, but this is the nearest measured number. (5) Cost sensitivity: a 10 bp spread/impact overrun on the alt leg (where Bianchi et al. locate the reversal premium) adds 6-16 bp/day at tau 0.6-1.6 -> raises IC* by 15-45%; 897's flat 5 bp adverse-selection term is the same order as the design's claimed 2.3 bp/unit maker-timing gain, so the execution component nets to ~0 or negative. (6) N_eff: the variance term 22.1/sqrt(N_eff) is 7.8 bp/day at 8 and 4.9 at 20 - against a 34.5 bp/day cost term at HL 6 h it is second-order; N_eff error cannot rescue the fast end, and a residual-of-(market+3 PCs) N_eff of 30-80 must be paired with the book's REALISED daily SD, not the theoretical 435/sqrt(N_eff). (7) Bounce magnitude: last-print hourly returns with relative spread s carry rho_1 ~ -(s^2/4)/(sigma_1h^2 + s^2/2); s = 50 bp, sigma_1h = 71 bp -> -0.10, concentrated in the illiquid tail -> a cross-sectional 'reversal IC' at h = 1-2 of order 0.05-0.1 that exceeds the required line and cannot be traded (the print is the bid).

LITERATURE NUMBERS: Fischer-Krauss-Deinert 2019 (abstract via Semantic Scholar, abstract-level): NET 7.1 bp/day after 15 bp/half-turn, OOS 2018-06-18..09-17 (3 months), 40 coins, 120-min horizon, top-3/flop-3 book, >100k trades, minute-binned (not Kraken), no Sharpe stated; 7.1 bp/day = 2.6%/yr on a 6-name L/S crypto book = Sharpe ~0.05-0.15 - the 'real, cost-bound' shape, not a clearing precedent, and the design's 'break-even 17-18 bp/side' is an inference (at 12 rebalances/day x ~1.4 turnover, break-even is ~15.4 bp). Kitron-Wengrowicz 2026 (arXiv 2608.21888 abstract, abstract-level): 15-min, 183 Binance pairs, gross ~1.3 bp/trade, 5 bp round-trip assumed, AUC gap +0.011 [+0.008,+0.014] conservative, 6-month frozen holdout, 'too small to clear benchmark spot capture costs' - matches design's citation; note Binance liquidity >> Kraken. Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson 2022 (abstract via Semantic Scholar, abstract-level): DAILY short-term reversal, 2017-03..2022-03, multi-exchange USD pairs, no magnitudes - a daily-horizon study cited for hourly structure. Nagel 2012: equities, daily/weekly reversal (from memory). GP 2013 formulas: consistent with my derivation of the EMA/aim structure; not re-read.
profit_source_check: Stated source: FORECAST of the first moment (market-residual, vol-standardised return over 1-24 h given rank features), with an explicitly separate cost-reduction component; the design states the iterated-expectations identity (zero conditional mean => net = -tau x 21 bp). As stated, honest. Three problems with what the instrument would actually attribute to that source: (1) At h = 1-2 h on a tape where BTC's mid is frozen 38.9% of the time (`handoff_run_50.md:72`) and alts far more, a large share of any measured 'reversal IC' is bid-ask bounce / stale last prints - a measurement artifact, not a conditional mean anyone can trade - and the guard the design pre-registers does not remove it (see record conflict 1); 806's own 'persistence' cell (IC -0.052 at H=1 min, `runs/806_predictability_probe/result.md` cell table) is the bounce signature already in the record, and 897 attributes the minute surface's death to exactly this ('the killer is adverse selection/immediacy'). (2) The 'cost reduction' component is measured against a strawman (raw hourly/daily re-ranking); against the daily GP book TASK_915 §4.2 already specifies it is 0-4% for HL >= 1 d - not a profit source, a restatement. (3) The maker-timing gain (2.3 bp/unit) is an upper bound assuming touch fills with no adverse selection; 897's measured 5 bp adverse-selection term is larger and of opposite sign. Is it a forecast in disguise of something already measured dead? Partly redundant rather than dead: the HL >= 1 d two-thirds of the band is TASK_915's h = 1, 3 d cells with GP smoothing (PROPOSED, not run); the HL < 12 h third is unmeasured with native features, but its nearest neighbours - 816 H=60/240 (gross Sharpe +2.03/+0.28 at turnover 1.40, net -107/-27 at 21 bp; minute-lag features), 897 (0/864 at any nonzero fee, <= 20 min), Kitron-Wengrowicz (15 min, 1.3 bp vs 5 bp) - all read 'real, cost-bound'. On the learning question: the design concedes it is pooled closed-form estimation; pooling 17M asset-hours into 40 coefficients is a legitimate variance argument, but the GBM arm is pre-registered to fail (811 prior) and no object here carries information a per-horizon ridge cannot - so 'learning' is not load-bearing, which also means the design does not answer the operator's brief (a learning mechanism that is not the memo's IC-ceiling + GP restated); it is that restatement at hourly cadence.

Entering at the open of t+1 is the first 1-min bar of the next hour, which on a stale tape is the same print as close of t (`trader/data.py:161-183`: period open = first bar's open, close = last bar's close; missing periods ffilled at :225-226 -> zero return). The guard as written cannot fail the bounce artifact, so the pre-registered 'IC under lag >= 70% of un-lagged' test would pass spuriously at h = 1-2 h.

surviving_mechanism: Not a book. The narrowest survivor is an hourly DIAGNOSTIC IC surface folded into TASK_915 as a second panel (the design's own composition note): h in {1,2,4,6,12} h, lookbacks 1 h-7 d, families F1-F3, ridge only (no GBM, no neural), reported with (i) a TRUE one-bar-skip entry (close of t+1, as 816 G8 actually does) and, as a second arm, entry at the first print >= 10 min into bar t+1; (ii) a stale-hour screen from trade_count (drop asset-hours whose last minute has zero trades; report the per-asset stale-hour fraction); (iii) a majors-only (top-30 dollar-volume) vs all-assets split so a pass cannot live only in the illiquid tail where 21 bp/side is fictional; (iv) the required-IC line computed per horizon in matching units on MEASURED tau, TC and the book's realised daily SD; (v) Bonferroni over every quoted cell plus SR0(N). Its value is to close the 1-12 h band on OHLC quantitatively (expected shape: IC 0.005-0.02, t >> 3, below the line). The HL >= 1 d cells are dropped as redundant with 915's daily GP. No controller, no execution layer, no book unless the lag-robust, stale-screened, majors-inclusive IC clears its line in each of 2024/2025.
kill_experiment_critique: Well-formed in its statistics (per-hour Spearman IC, NW lag h, Bonferroni over fitted cells, block-Rademacher/circular-shift placebos, SR0(N) beside every table, one pre-declared book, daily-aggregated Sharpe) but defective in the places that decide the answer. (1) The bounce guard is vacuous: 'open of t+1' equals 'close of t' on a stale tape and is not what 816 G8 did (probe.py:209,218-220); as written G-A's 'lag-robust >= 70%' test passes the artifact. Fix: enter at close(t+1) or first print >= 10 min into t+1, plus a trade_count stale screen; pre-register that a cell whose IC falls > 50% under the true skip is dead. (2) Units: IC*_h = (504·tau + 22.1/sqrt(N_eff))/(2130·TC) is an IC_1h line, but G-A compares 'mean IC' of h = 2, 4, 6 h cells to it; without the horizon conversion IC_h ~ IC_1h·(1-rho^h)/((1-rho)sqrt(h)) a longer-h cell passes by construction. (3) The variance term must use the book's realised daily SD, not 435/sqrt(N_eff) with an N_eff computed on 4-factor residuals (30-80) - otherwise the line is lowered by 3-5 bp/day on paper. (4) Cost model: 21 bp/side flat on alts at hourly cadence is the design's own stated weakest assumption yet no cost arm exists; add a spread-proxy arm (e.g., half the hourly range or 907's markout for majors) and the majors/all split; without it a G-A pass -> G-B fail is attributed to 'control' when it is the cost model. (5) G-A lets a GBM cell pass alone; with the 811 prior a GBM pass over a ridge fail is a multiplicity signature - require ridge within 20% or flag. (6) 288 descriptive cells (8 L x 6 h x 3 families x 2 lags) are reported without multiplicity; any quoted as a finding needs Bonferroni/SR0. (7) 2026 is one quarter (899 seam) - a positivity-by-year gate on it is under-powered; make it sign-only. (8) 'G-A pass / G-B fail is the only legitimate re-entry for a search-based controller' is not licensed by the turnover decomposition, which cannot separate controller suboptimality from cost-model error. (9) Two-thirds of the grid (HL >= 1 d) duplicates TASK_915 at 24x the rows; restrict the new claim to h <= 12 h and run it as 915's second panel to keep one IC estimator and one multiplicity account. Compute claim (<= 2 CPU-days, no GPU) is right; the 64 GB cards are irrelevant, as the design says.
odds_after_refutation: P(G-A as WRITTEN passes) ~ 15-20%, mostly via the unguarded h = 1-2 h bounce artifact - a false pass. P(a genuine, true-skip-robust, stale-screened, majors-inclusive cell in the 1-12 h band clears its measured required line, NW t >= 3, positive in 2024 and 2025) ~ 4-6% (design said 12%). P(G-B +0.97 net@21 PIT 2024-26 | genuine G-A) ~ 25-30% (alt spread/impact above 21 bp, shortability and unmodelled Kraken margin rollover on the short leg, TC/turnover worse than the AR(1) closed form on a non-exponential decay). Unconditional P(+0.97 net@21, PIT, 2024-26) ~ 1.5-2%; P(>= +0.56) ~ 3-4%. Most likely outcome (~60%): hourly IC 0.005-0.02 in the band, detectable at t >> 3, below the line - the same 'real, cost-bound' shape as 806/811/816/897 below it and 819/898 above it. Value of the surviving diagnostic is unchanged and real: it closes the last unmeasured OHLC horizon band two-sidedly for ~1 CPU-day inside TASK_915, and its FAIL composes with 915's G-A fail into the memo's pre-committed D4 repeal.
